newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Illegal immigrants riot in Lithuanian camp.
newsitem.headline: Illegal immigrants riot in Lithuanian camp.

text.p: Lithuanian officials began talks with illegal immigrants at a refugee camp on Thursday after hundreds of detainees rioted late on Wednesday, beating up two guards in a protest at restrictive conditions.
"Though we are now controlling the situation, we are sitting on a powder keg," the camp's director, Evaldas Stuinyla, told Reuters by telephone.
He said the protesters were well organised and had surrounded the camp's administrative headquarters during the rioting.
The camp in the bleak eastern Lithuanian town of Pabrade houses 626 illegal immigrants, mainly from countries like Pakistan, Sri Lanka, India and Iraq.
Since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, Lithuania and its Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia have become a conduit for economic migrants attempting to reach the affluent Nordic countries.
The inmates were mainly protesting at new restrictions on their movements, Stuinyla said. The unrest subsided when riot police arrived and officials promised to continue negotiations.

The Baltic states have faced censure over their treatment of refugees in the past and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said the riots highlighted the need for a less authoritarian regime at the centre.

"As far as I understand, they had not been allowed to visit the town for a few days and so the situation evolved incrementally," Linas Sesickas, the UNHCR's liaison officer in Lithuania, told Reuters.
In 1995, a group of more than 100 Asian refugees were shuttled back and forth across the Lithuanian, Latvian and Russian borders for several weeks on what observers dubbed the "train of tears."
